benchmarks.name: Campagne et al. 2015, P. oceanica, carbon excluded
benchmarks.note: The primary valuation behind four of the ledger's services (coastal protection, water purification, fisheries, bioindicator and knowledge). Gaia is above it because the ledger adds recreational diving and non-use values (Step 8c.2) and the food the meadow's primary production supports beyond the commercial catch (Step 8e.6).
benchmarks.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2

benchmarks.name: Campagne et al. 2015, P. oceanica, carbon included
benchmarks.note: Carbon sequestration 7.7-230 €/ha/yr at 35 €/t CO2; 11 of 25 services unvalued (mainly tourism and cultural).
benchmarks.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061

benchmarks.name: Stamatiadou et al. 2025, Mediterranean seagrass meta-regression (country range)
benchmarks.note: Basin mean 8,712; range across countries (Morocco to Monaco). 17 studies, 91 observations, 8 services incl. recreation and climate regulation; values scale with GDP per capita.
benchmarks.source: Stamatiadou, Mazaris & Katsanevakis (2025), Ecosystem Services 72:101704, doi:10.1016/j.ecoser.2025.101704

benchmarks.name: de Groot et al. 2012 (ESVD/TEEB), coastal systems
benchmarks.note: Central: total of the per-service means (28 estimates); range: totals of the per-service minima and maxima. Coastal systems, not seagrass alone.
benchmarks.source: de Groot et al. (2012), Ecosystem Services 1:50-61, doi:10.1016/j.ecoser.2012.07.005, as tabulated by Costanza et al. (2014) Table 4

benchmarks.name: Costanza et al. 2014, seagrass/algae beds
benchmarks.note: Global unit value; 26,223 of it is nutrient cycling.
benchmarks.source: Costanza et al. (2014), Global Environmental Change 26:152-158, doi:10.1016/j.gloenvcha.2014.04.002, Table 3

benchmarks.method: Benchmarks in their own currency and price year, not converted: an order-of-magnitude comparison. Gaia's carbon release (a stock, released at once or over time) is not in any per-hectare yearly figure.

calibration.calibration_regime_meaning: B (direct effects only): damage curves are read as each agent's direct dependency, interaction edges add the indirect part

parameters.name: model.trophic_transfer_efficiency
parameters.note: Midpoint of the 5-20% energy transfer efficiency between trophic levels (the textbook range following Lindeman 1942; from memory, verify). The midpoint is a choice, not a measurement.

parameters.name: model.trophic_amplification_exponent
parameters.note: No source: damps the pyramid ratio to 1.6-4.1× amplification for trophic levels 1-3.

parameters.name: model.keystone_edge_multiplier
parameters.note: No source: outgoing edge strengths of a collapsed keystone agent are multiplied by this factor.

parameters.name: carbon_price.year0
parameters.note: Social cost of carbon. The 2020-emissions value is used as the year-0 price: EPA's own path gives about $215 for 2026 emissions, so year-0 carbon damage is understated by about 13%. 2020 euros, no inflation adjustment.
parameters.source: US EPA (2023), Report on the Social Cost of Greenhouse Gases, Table ES.1: $190/tCO2 (2020 emissions, 2020 USD, 2% near-term rate), at the ECB 2020 average rate of 1.1422 USD/EUR

parameters.name: carbon_price.growth
parameters.note: 60-year average of a decelerating path (1.6%/yr in 2020-2050, 1.2%/yr in 2030-2080).

parameters.name: resource.area_ha
parameters.note: replaces the case default 4582 ha (medium)
parameters.source: user-supplied (--hectares / total_hectares)

parameters.name: resource.unit_value
parameters.note: Project-specific input: the private gain per hectare of meadow destroyed (one-off), which the user sets with --unit-value for the project assessed. 2,500 is the former owner specification, kept as an illustration; no source can make it general.

parameters.name: resource.safe_threshold_ratio
parameters.note: No ecological or regulatory source supports a 'safe' loss of 20% of a priority habitat (Habitats Directive 1120*): the value is the former owner specification. Under the case's area_loss damage model (Step 8c.3) it is the depletion of the reference resource beyond which the REMAINING meadow starts to degrade; below it each hectare lost costs exactly its average per-hectare value (linear benefit transfer). Monte Carlo range 0.1-0.3, uniform (judgement).

parameters.name: agent[Posidonia Meadow].annual_value_per_ha
parameters.note: Service ledger (Step 8e.6, 8f.1; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2b): the meadow's own value on EVERY hectare, whatever the diving: the food its primary production supports, 426.29 EUR/ha/yr gross (NPP 476 g DW = 160 g C/m2/yr → 74% into the food web → 14.3% transfer per trophic level (Western Mediterranean food-web models) to trophic level 3.1 → x9 wet weight → 46.5% sustainable catch → EUR 5.11/kg), net of the 35 EUR/ha/yr of commercial catch already booked to Fish Populations and Marine Invertebrates: 391.29 EUR/ha/yr. Weight x value = that net service. No site share or --dive-intensity scales it, so the meadow never falls to EUR 0 (PROJECT_DEFINITION.md, Core Valuation Principles). Range: the chain at every link's least and most favourable end (22.71-1,837.96 EUR/ha/yr), divided by the weight.
parameters.source: Service ledger, production function (Step 8e.6): Pergent et al. (1994), doi:10.3354/meps106139; Duarte (1990), doi:10.3354/meps067201; Mateo & Romero (1997), doi:10.3354/meps151043; Coll et al. (2008), doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0003881; Francour (1997), doi:10.1111/j.1439-0485.1997.tb00434.x with FishBase; Pauly & Christensen (1995), doi:10.1038/374255a0; Zhou et al. (2012), doi:10.1139/f2012-060; Generalitat de Catalunya fisheries statistics (dataset ge3m-4jgm); see production_function

parameters.name: agent[Coralligenous & Red Coral].annual_value_per_ha
parameters.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): recreational diving on the coralligenous, 18.95 EUR/ha/yr = EUR 60 per dive x 60,000 Medes dives a year / 190,000 ha of mapped seabed. A Catalan primary study; the attribution to a hectare of meadow is the seascape rule used for every service of the wider seascape: the regional value spread evenly over the mapped seabed. PROVISIONAL: an attribution assumption, not a source (no study links coralligenous condition to the nearby meadow), accepted by the owner as provisional (Step 8d.3) until an area-weighted link to nearby reefs can be sourced. Range 9.5-43.8 EUR/ha/yr: half the attribution to EUR 108.01/dive (Zunino et al. 2020, total loss of coralligenous) x 77,000 dives.
parameters.source: Rodrigues, van den Bergh, Loureiro, Nunes & Rossi (2016), Environmental and Resource Economics 63:289-311, doi:10.1007/s10640-015-9935-8: choice experiment with scuba divers at the Medes Islands MPA (Catalonia); the local extinction of gorgonians, the emblem of the coralligenous, costs divers about EUR 60 per dive; about 60,000 dives a year at the Medes Islands: Ràdio Capital de l'Empordà (26 May 2026, reporting the Parc Natural del Montgrí, les Illes Medes i el Baix Ter / SUBMON study: 'prop de 60.000 immersions anuals'); the former annual cap was 60,000 and the 2015 plan raised it to almost 77,000 (Ara, 19 June 2015); ~190,000 ha of seabed mapped to 50 m (Generalitat 2025 marine habitat map, as reported by Ara, 29 May 2025; see resource.area_ha)

parameters.name: agent[Epiphytes & Algae].annual_value_per_ha
parameters.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): an intermediate agent with no final service of its own: it owns the epiphyte share of the bioindicator service, moved from Human Communities (total unchanged): 1.5 x 0.5/3.5 = 0.2143 EUR/ha/yr, the weight of the epiphyte/leaf biomass metric in the PREI index used to monitor P. oceanica. Range x0.5-x2 (judgement).
parameters.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): use as bioindicator 1.5 EUR/ha/yr; share: Gobert et al. (2009), Marine Pollution Bulletin 58:1727-1733, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2009.06.012, PREI EQR' = (N density + N leaf surface + N(E/L) + N lower limit)/3.5 with N(E/L) = [1 - E/L] x 0.5

parameters.name: agent[Marine Invertebrates].annual_value_per_ha
parameters.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): the invertebrate share of the fisheries service, moved from Fish Populations (total unchanged): 35 x 2/16 = 4.375 EUR/ha/yr, by species count (2 of Campagne et al.'s 16 species; equal value per species is an assumption). Range 3.4-18.8 EUR/ha/yr: 27 x 2/16 to 74 x 0.254, the cephalopod and other-invertebrate share of Catalan white-fish, cephalopod and other-invertebrate first-sale value in 2014 (Generalitat, Estadístiques de pesca per grups biològics, dataset ge3m-4jgm: EUR 13.65 M + 0.34 M against 41.06 M; a proxy, not meadow-specific).
parameters.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): fishery contribution 27-35 EUR/ha/yr from 16 meadow-associated species sold at the Sète auction, two of them invertebrates (Paracentrotus lividus, Sepia officinalis), §3.2.4

parameters.name: agent[Fish Populations].annual_value_per_ha
parameters.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): the fish share of the fisheries service, 35 x 14/16 = 30.625 EUR/ha/yr (14 of the 16 species are fish; the two invertebrates go to Marine Invertebrates). Range 23.6-64.8 EUR/ha/yr: (27 to 74) x 14/16. 74 is derived here, not published: Jackson et al. (2015, Conservation Biology 29:899-909, doi:10.1111/cobi.12436) attribute EUR 58-91 million/yr of Mediterranean commercial landings to seagrass; divided by the known P. oceanica area, 1,224,707 ha (Telesca et al. 2015, Scientific Reports 5:12505, doi:10.1038/srep12505), that is EUR 47-74/ha/yr (an overestimate per ha of P. oceanica).
parameters.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): fishery contribution 27-35 EUR/ha/yr (production function); upper end used

parameters.name: agent[Marine Megafauna].annual_value_per_ha
parameters.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): non-use value of protecting marine mammals (dolphins) and, by extension, sea turtles, 30.18 EUR/ha/yr: the 5-year payment of GBP 30.32 annualised at the case's 2.3% (GBP 3.26/yr in perpetuity), converted at 0.84926 GBP/EUR (EUR 3.84), times 2,989,357 Catalan households (EUR 11.5 M/yr), spread over 190,000 ha of mapped seabed (the seascape rule, PROVISIONAL: an attribution assumption accepted by the owner as provisional, Step 8d.3) and split equally between Marine Megafauna and Seabirds, which Börger et al.'s attribute bundles. A unit-value benefit transfer from the UK (no income adjustment) of a protection scenario (50% of an area) read as the value at full damage: a lower bound in scope, an uncertain transfer. Range x0.33-x3 (judgement).
parameters.source: Börger, Hattam, Burdon, Atkins & Austen (2014), Ecological Economics 108:229-241, doi:10.1016/j.ecolecon.2014.10.006: choice experiment, UK households pay GBP 30.32/yr (mixed logit; 5-year tax) to protect porpoises, seals and seabirds on 50% of the UK Dogger Bank (GBP 24.02 on 25%); 2,989,357 households in Catalonia (Idescat, Households by size, 2021, from the INE Population and Housing Census); ~190,000 ha of seabed mapped to 50 m (Generalitat 2025 marine habitat map, as reported by Ara, 29 May 2025; see resource.area_ha); ECB euro reference rate, GBP per EUR, 2013 annual average 0.84926

parameters.name: agent[Seabirds].annual_value_per_ha
parameters.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): non-use value of protecting seabirds (Audouin's gull, shags, shearwaters), 30.18 EUR/ha/yr: the 5-year payment of GBP 30.32 annualised at the case's 2.3% (GBP 3.26/yr in perpetuity), converted at 0.84926 GBP/EUR (EUR 3.84), times 2,989,357 Catalan households (EUR 11.5 M/yr), spread over 190,000 ha of mapped seabed (the seascape rule, PROVISIONAL: an attribution assumption accepted by the owner as provisional, Step 8d.3) and split equally between Marine Megafauna and Seabirds, which Börger et al.'s attribute bundles. A unit-value benefit transfer from the UK (no income adjustment) of a protection scenario (50% of an area) read as the value at full damage: a lower bound in scope, an uncertain transfer. Range x0.33-x3 (judgement).
parameters.source: Börger, Hattam, Burdon, Atkins & Austen (2014), Ecological Economics 108:229-241, doi:10.1016/j.ecolecon.2014.10.006: choice experiment, UK households pay GBP 30.32/yr (mixed logit; 5-year tax) to protect porpoises, seals and seabirds on 50% of the UK Dogger Bank (GBP 24.02 on 25%); 2,989,357 households in Catalonia (Idescat, Households by size, 2021, from the INE Population and Housing Census); ~190,000 ha of seabed mapped to 50 m (Generalitat 2025 marine habitat map, as reported by Ara, 29 May 2025; see resource.area_ha); ECB euro reference rate, GBP per EUR, 2013 annual average 0.84926

parameters.name: agent[Coastal Protection].annual_value_per_ha
parameters.note: 188 EUR/ha/yr of service at full damage = weight × value (service ledger, Step 8c.2) (188 / 0.142857). A single estimate; it covers wave attenuation, beach-cast banquettes and matte sediment stabilisation (Campagne et al.'s three services). Its spread in the Monte Carlo (×/÷2) is a judgement.
parameters.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): protection from coastal erosion 188 EUR/ha/yr (damage cost avoided, Mediterranean scale, 2001 data inflated to 2014)

parameters.name: agent[Water Quality].annual_value_per_ha
parameters.note: 60 EUR/ha/yr of service at full damage = weight × value (service ledger, Step 8c.2) (60 / 0.120879). A single, crude benefit-transfer estimate. Its spread in the Monte Carlo (×/÷2) is a judgement.
parameters.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): wastewater treatment 60 EUR/ha/yr (benefit transfer of the French water-protection tax, one third attributed to coastal systems after Costanza et al. 1997)

parameters.name: agent[Human Communities].annual_value_per_ha
parameters.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): bioindicator use without its epiphyte share (1.5 x 3/3.5) + knowledge contribution 0.33 = 1.6157 EUR/ha/yr. Beach tourism is still NOT valued (no Posidonia-specific welfare estimate); recreational-fisheries expenditure (EUR 112 million/yr for Mediterranean seagrass, Jackson et al. 2015) is spending, not welfare, and is not used. Its spread in the Monte Carlo (x/÷2) is a judgement.
parameters.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): bioindicator use 1.5 + knowledge contribution 0.33 EUR/ha/yr; the epiphyte share of the bioindicator (0.5/3.5 of the PREI, Gobert et al. 2009, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2009.06.012) moved to Epiphytes & Algae

parameters.name: agent[Posidonia Meadow].site_value_per_ha
parameters.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; restricted to dive sites in Step 8d.4; site_value_per_ha since Step 8e.6; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): recreational diving amenity of the meadow, PER HECTARE OF MEADOW WITHIN REACH OF DIVE SITES, on top of the meadow's value on every hectare (annual_value_per_ha): 14,630.14 EUR/ha/yr = EUR 34.71 per dive x 60,000 Medes dives a year / 142.35 ha of meadow near Costa Brava dive sites. A run multiplies it by site_share, the share of the affected meadow near dive sites: the regional default 142.35 / 4,582 = 0.0311 gives the regional average, 454.52 EUR/ha/yr (the former value); a project states its own (--dive-site-share: 1 at a dive site, 0 far from any). The value is stated at the Costa Brava's average diving intensity, 60,000 / 142.35 = 421.5 dives per hectare of meadow near dive sites per year (site_intensity); a project can state the intensity at its meadow (--dive-intensity none/low/medium/high, Step 8e.2), which scales it by level / 421.5. Unit-value benefit transfer of a per-dive WTP from Italian to Catalan divers (no income adjustment); it assumes every Medes dive includes meadow (an upper bias) and counts no dives at the other Costa Brava sites, whose numbers were not found (a lower bias). Range 6,874-41,651 EUR/ha/yr near dive sites (214-1,294 at the regional share): EUR 18.12/dive (the 50%-loss value, i.e. half the dives over meadow) x 54,000 dives to EUR 77/dive (latent class 1, total loss) x 77,000 dives (the plan's cap), over 142.35 ha; the uncertainty of the 142.35 ha is not sampled (at the regional share it cancels out). Weight x value = the service near dive sites.
parameters.source: Zunino, Melaku Canu, Marangon & Troiano (2020), Frontiers in Marine Science 6:823, doi:10.3389/fmars.2019.00823: choice experiment with 221 Italian scuba divers (2016-17); a total loss of P. oceanica cover lowers the willingness to pay for a dive by about EUR 34 (MNL, Table 3: -34.71); about 60,000 dives a year at the Medes Islands: Ràdio Capital de l'Empordà (26 May 2026, reporting the Parc Natural del Montgrí, les Illes Medes i el Baix Ter / SUBMON study: 'prop de 60.000 immersions anuals'); the former annual cap was 60,000 and the 2015 plan raised it to almost 77,000 (Ara, 19 June 2015); meadow within reach of dive sites: 142.35 ha, the P. oceanica cover of the Costa Brava's coastal Natura 2000 sites (EEA Natura 2000 Standard Data Forms, see site_restricted.share)

parameters.name: agent[Posidonia Meadow].site_share
parameters.note: The share of the affected meadow within reach of dive sites, where the meadow's diving value applies (Step 8d.4). A PROJECT INPUT: the user states it with --dive-site-share (1 for a project at a dive site, 0 far from any; recorded as user-supplied). The default is the regional share: 142.35 ha near dive sites / 4,582 ha, the expected share for a meadow of unknown location. The 142.35 ha are a proxy, flagged: the P. oceanica cover inside the coastal Natura 2000 sites of the Costa Brava, which hold its best-known dive sites (Medes Islands, Cap de Creus; dive sites elsewhere in these sites assumed, not verified); a site boundary is not the reach of a dive site, and the 2014 forms and the 2025 regional map differ in date and method. Held fixed in the Monte Carlo ("distribution": "fixed").
parameters.source: European Environment Agency, Natura 2000 Standard Data Forms, habitat 1120* (Posidonia beds) cover in ha, forms last updated December 2014, via the EEA Natura 2000 service (https://bio.discomap.eea.europa.eu/arcgis/rest/services/Bio/Natura2000_Dyna_WM/MapServer/13, queried 12 October 2026; site pages https://natura2000.eea.europa.eu/Natura2000/SDF.aspx?site=ES5120007 etc.): Cap de Creus (ES5120007) 64.14 ha, El Montgrí-Les Medes-El Baix Ter (ES5120016) 10.75 ha, Litoral del Baix Empordà (ES5120015) 24.10 ha, Massís de les Cadiretes (ES5120013) 42.36 ha, L'Albera (ES5120014) 1.00 ha: 142.35 ha in the coastal Natura 2000 sites of the Costa Brava (Girona coast); cross-check: the Medes Islands meadow covers 8.8 ha (Romero, Pérez & Renom 2001, Seguimiento de la pradera de Posidonia oceanica de las islas Medes, Ejercicio 2001, Universitat de Barcelona, http://hdl.handle.net/2445/25506); regional stock 4,582 ha (resource.area_ha)

parameters.name: agent[Posidonia Meadow].site_intensity
parameters.note: The diving intensity at which the meadow's near-site value is stated (Step 8e.2): 60,000 / 142.35 = 421.5 dives per hectare of meadow near dive sites per year, the Costa Brava average (only the Medes dives are counted, a lower bias). A PROJECT INPUT through the levels of site_intensity_levels: --dive-intensity {none,low,medium,high} scales the near-site value by level / 421.5 (none 0, low 66.2, medium 566.5, high 5,581 dives/ha/yr) and is recorded as user-supplied. Held fixed in the Monte Carlo ("distribution": "fixed"); the meadow's value keeps its own relative range at any level.
parameters.source: about 60,000 dives a year at the Medes Islands (Ràdio Capital de l'Empordà, 26 May 2026, reporting the Parc Natural del Montgrí, les Illes Medes i el Baix Ter / SUBMON study) / 142.35 ha of P. oceanica within reach of the Costa Brava's dive sites (EEA Natura 2000 Standard Data Forms, see site_share)

parameters.name: damage.threshold_logistic_steepness
parameters.note: Degradation of the remaining meadow past the safe threshold (damage model area_loss, Step 8c.3): zero up to the threshold, then a logistic with its inflection 15% into the post-threshold span (32% loss at the default threshold), the same curve for every agent. The damage of each agent is D + (1 - D) x degradation, so its slope at small losses is exactly 1 (each hectare lost costs its average value) and the curve shapes only the threshold behaviour. No Posidonia study relates the fraction of a meadow lost to the degradation of the rest, so the curve is not fitted (calibration regime B). Monte Carlo range 6-18, uniform (judgement).

parameters.name: agent[Posidonia Meadow].keystone_threshold
parameters.note: Health below which the meadow's outgoing edges double; hand-set, no source. Monte Carlo range 0.15-0.45, uniform (judgement).

parameters.name: edge[Posidonia Meadow → Coralligenous & Red Coral].strength

The links themselves are documented (e.g. meadow -> wave attenuation: Infantes et al. 2012, MEPS 456:63-72, doi:10.3354/meps09754; seagrass -> fisheries: Jackson et al. 2015), their strengths are not. Monte Carlo range: ×0.5 to ×1.5 (judgement; wider ranges breach the in-degree cap).

parameters.name: carbon.stored_carbon_tonnes
parameters.note: Living biomass is not counted separately: the leaves are negligible next to the matte, and the living rhizomes and roots lie inside the top-metre matte stock counted in soil_carbon_tonnes (counting them here too would double count). No Posidonia leaf-biomass carbon figure was verified for this review.
parameters.source: Label Bas-Carbone, 'Méthode de protection des herbiers de posidonie' (French Ministry of Ecological Transition, approved 21 March 2023, NOR ENER2305073S; https://aida.ineris.fr/sites/aida/files/2023-04/Dec20230321_1.pdf), §7: the carbon in the living leaves is 'négligeable comparé au carbone stocké et séquestré dans la matte'

parameters.name: carbon.annual_absorption_tonnes
parameters.note: S5 resolved: one long-term burial (sequestration) rate, from the nearest region with direct measurements. Range 0.28-3.09 tCO2/ha/yr: 7.7-84.4 g C/m2/yr, the depth range of mean sequestration in a large Corsican meadow (Pergent-Martini et al. 2021, Marine Environmental Research 165:105236, doi:10.1016/j.marenvres.2020.105236). The former value, 1.58 tCO2/ha/yr, was the IPCC (2013) Wetlands Supplement Table 4.12 seagrass factor (0.434 t C/ha/yr, 95% CI 0.2-0.7, from Mateo & Romero 1997 and Serrano et al. 2012), which applies to revegetated meadows; it lies inside the range.
parameters.source: Mazarrasa et al. (2017), Limnology and Oceanography 62:1436-1450, doi:10.1002/lno.10510: organic carbon burial 26 ± 6 g C/m2/yr in Balearic P. oceanica meadows since 1900 (210Pb-dated cores) = 0.26 t C/ha/yr × 44/12

parameters.name: carbon.soil_carbon_tonnes
parameters.note: Organic carbon in the top metre of matte (the depth IPCC and the Label Bas-Carbone method treat as exposed), not the whole matte, which can be several metres thick. Range 741-1,844 tCO2/ha: 20.2-50.3 kg Corg/m2 in the first metre of matte in Calvi Bay (Leduc et al. 2023, Marine Environmental Research 183:105847, doi:10.1016/j.marenvres.2022.105847). Corsican, not Catalan, measurements; for scale, the IPCC (2013) global Tier 1 seagrass soil stock is 108 t C/ha to 1 m (Table 4.11) and Balearic P. oceanica holds 6.1 ± 1.4 kg C/m2 in the top 30 cm alone (Mazarrasa et al. 2017).
parameters.source: Monnier et al. (2022), Science of the Total Environment 838:155864, doi:10.1016/j.scitotenv.2022.155864 (39 matte cores, eastern Corsica: 327 ± 150 t Corg/ha), adopted as the Tier 1 default for 1 m of matte by Label Bas-Carbone, 'Méthode de protection des herbiers de posidonie' (French Ministry of Ecological Transition, approved 21 March 2023, NOR ENER2305073S; https://aida.ineris.fr/sites/aida/files/2023-04/Dec20230321_1.pdf); × 44/12

parameters.name: carbon.soil_release_fraction
parameters.note: A project input (--carbon-release-fraction): it depends on what the project does to the matte. Recommended values (docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §4): excavated or dredged (port basins, channels) 0.96, the IPCC (2013) Wetlands Supplement Tier 1 for 'excavation to enable port, harbour and marina construction' (the top-metre soil carbon emitted in the year of extraction, minus 4% refractory); left exposed in place (meadow killed by shading, turbidity, anchoring or scour) 0.25-1.0, central 0.63 (this value, Pendleton et al.'s global range); buried under fill (breakwaters, reclaimed land) no source was found: the anoxic matte may keep much of its carbon (inferred, not sourced). The Label Bas-Carbone method models anchoring damage as a gradual loss (10.7% of the top-metre carbon over 10 years, after Mateo et al. 2019). The dominant uncertainty of the carbon externality.
parameters.source: Pendleton et al. (2012), PLoS ONE 7:e43542, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0043542: 25-100% of near-surface (top-metre) carbon lost upon conversion, central estimate 63%

parameters.name: carbon.release_half_life_years
parameters.note: A project input (--carbon-release-half-life): the time profile of the release, valued year by year at the carbon price of that year and discounted. 10 years is the upper end of Pendleton et al.'s order of magnitude; seagrass evidence brackets it: the exposed share of Shark Bay's seagrass soil carbon was estimated released within three years of the 2010/11 die-off (Arias-Ortiz et al. 2018, Nature Climate Change 8:338-344, doi:10.1038/s41558-018-0096-y); soil stocks were 72% lower 50 years after a disturbance (Macreadie et al. 2015, Proc. R. Soc. B 282:20151537, doi:10.1098/rspb.2015.1537), i.e. a half-life of at most 27 years if the decay were exponential (inferred here); 4.8 of 6.4 kg Corg/m2 of the top 50 cm were lost under moorings deployed from the 1930s (Serrano et al. 2016, Sci. Rep. 6:23193, doi:10.1038/srep23193). Excavated matte: 0 (the IPCC emits it in the year of extraction). Range 0-27 years (judgement from these sources).
parameters.source: Pendleton et al. (2012), PLoS ONE 7:e43542, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0043542: at a converted site the rate of release 'likely follows a negative exponential curve with time', with 'a half-life on the order of 5-10 years' (their ref. 29, a cleared mangrove)

parameters.name: discount.rate_schedule[year 0]
parameters.note: The rate is the experts' mean recommendation, not a Ramsey sum: the survey's Ramsey components (median δ 0.5%, mean η 1.35, mean growth 1.70%) do not add up to it, and the former g = 1.3% had no source. parameters.name: discount.scarcity_rate
parameters.note: The Netherlands' default relative price change for all ecosystem services, as reported by Drupp et al. (2024, arXiv:2308.04400v3, §1; checked). agents.description: The meadow itself, keystone foundation species and one of the most productive habitats of the sea; its own final services: the food its primary production supports (production function, net of the commercial catch booked to fish and invertebrates), on every hectare, and the underwater amenity divers enjoy (Zunino et al. 2020), only where the meadow is within reach of dive sites
agents.name: Posidonia Meadow
value_notes: Primary production → food: NPP 160 g C/m²/yr (476 g dry weight) → 1,184 kg C/ha/yr into the food web → 179 kg fish and invertebrates/ha/yr (trophic level 3.1) → 83.4 kg/ha/yr sustainable catch × €5.11/kg = €426/ha/yr; minus €35.0 already counted (commercial catch, under Fish Populations, Marine Invertebrates) = €391/ha/yr
Carbon: 1,199 tCO2/ha held in the matte and 0.95 tCO2/ha/yr buried: valued once, in the carbon accounting, and not added to this line

ecosystem.name: Posidonia oceanica meadows of Catalonia (Costa Brava)

resource.carbon_price_basis: social cost of carbon, US EPA 2023
resource.name: Posidonia oceanica meadows of Catalonia (Costa Brava)

notes: Marine externality costs are ANNUAL (€/yr): they recur every year the meadow is gone. P. oceanica rhizomes grow only centimetres a year and a model of natural recolonisation leaves limited cover after a century (Kendrick et al. 2005), so loss is effectively permanent on human timescales. The net social cost compares the one-off private gain with the present value of these annual losses and of the carbon released. Every agent's euro value is a final ecosystem service booked once in the case's service ledger (Step 8c.2), and no input brings an agent to €0: the meadow's own value is the food its primary production supports (a production function, Step 8e.6), on every hectare; beach tourism and the meadow's own non-use value are still not valued, so the services total remains a lower bound.

pricing.derived_prices_note: No anchor of their own: each price is derived from the anchored agents upstream through the placeholder edge strengths (Step 8c.6).
pricing.note: EXPERIMENTAL (decision D4, C8): endogenous pricing is quarantined. Every price is certified convergent (a run that cannot be certified fails instead of falling back to static values), but the formulation counts upstream value once per dependent agent and prices the whole loss at the end-state scarcity price, and most shipped anchors are placeholders. Do not use these figures as estimates.

comparison.note: Gross production of whole communities, the comparable measure across these sources. The chain above starts from the plant's net production alone (160 g C/m²/yr: no roots, no epiphytes, no other algae), which is not comparable with these figures. Per hectare, seagrass meadows fix carbon on the scale of coral reefs and intensively farmed land; the Corsican P. oceanica meadow, measured over 12 years, fixes about half the seagrass average and 15 times the bare sediment around it.

carbon_fraction.label: carbon content of seagrass dry weight
carbon_fraction.source: Duarte (1990), Marine Ecology Progress Series 67:201-207, doi:10.3354/meps067201 (abstract): mean carbon content of seagrass leaves 33.6 ± 0.31% of dry weight (27 species, 30 locations); applied to sheaths and rhizomes as well

catch_trophic_level.label: mean trophic level of the catch
catch_trophic_level.source: Francour (1997), Marine Ecology 18:157-173, doi:10.1111/j.1439-0485.1997.tb00434.x (abstract): P. oceanica fish assemblages at Port-Cros dominated by Symphodus ocellatus, S. tinca, Diplodus annularis and Sarpa salpa; FishBase trophic levels from diet studies (fishbase.se, queried 13 October 2026) 3.5, 3.3, 3.6, 2.0: mean 3.1. Upper end 3.5: the median over 13 meadow species with the main targets (D. vulgaris 3.5, D. sargus 3.4, Mullus surmuletus 3.5, Scorpaena porcus 3.9, S. scrofa 4.3, Spondyliosoma cantharus 3.3, Labrus merula 3.6, Serranus scriba 3.8, Oblada melanura 3.4). The choice of species is a judgement

first_sale_price.label: first-sale price of bony white fish, Catalonia, 2014
first_sale_price.source: Generalitat de Catalunya, Estadístiques de pesca: dades per grups biològics (open data, dataset ge3m-4jgm, https://analisi.transparenciacatalunya.cat/resource/ge3m-4jgm.json, queried 13 October 2026): 'OSSIS-BLANC' 2014, EUR 41,056,589 for 8,034,993 kg = EUR 5.11/kg; EUR 2014, the price year of the fisheries value it is net of

food_web_share.label: share of the production eaten, decomposed or exported (to beaches and deep water) rather than buried in the matte
food_web_share.source: Mateo & Romero (1997), Marine Ecology Progress Series 151:43-53, doi:10.3354/meps151043 (abstract): about 26% of the carbon the plant produces in a year is buried below ground, Medes Islands (Catalonia), so 74% is not. Range: 71%, Pergent et al. (1994, doi:10.3354/meps106139, abstract: 42% degraded in place, 29% exported, 29% buried in the matte); 83.2%, Cebrián, Duarte, Marbà & Enríquez (1997), Marine Ecology Progress Series 155:29-44, doi:10.3354/meps155029 (abstract: 16.8% of P. oceanica production neither consumed nor decomposed in its first year, Cala Jonquet, Catalonia). Mateo & Romero add that most of it reaches animals through the detritus and its microbes (48% lost as very fine particles, 17% respired), not directly: the transfer efficiency of the next link carries that loss

npp_dry_weight.label: net primary production of the plant: leaf blades, sheaths and rhizomes (roots and epiphytes not included)
npp_dry_weight.source: Pergent, Romero, Pergent-Martini, Mateo & Boudouresque (1994), Marine Ecology Progress Series 106:139-146, doi:10.3354/meps106139 (abstract): blades 167-530, sheaths 51-142, rhizomes 20-42 g dry weight/m2/yr at 3 sites in Lacco Ameno Bay (Ischia, Italy); value = the sum of the midpoints (348.5 + 96.5 + 31), range = the sums of the minima and of the maxima. Not Catalan: the Cala Jonquet (Cap de Creus) production of Cebrián et al. (1997) was not readable (full text behind a bot check)

sustainable_catch_share.label: share of the production that can be caught sustainably (exploitation rate at maximum sustainable yield)
sustainable_catch_share.source: Zhou, Yin, Thorson, Smith & Fuller (2012), Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 69:1292-1301, doi:10.1139/f2012-060 (abstract): F_MSY = 0.87 M for teleosts (245 species); F proxy about 15% smaller; the rule of thumb F_MSY = M. Exploitation rate E = F/(F + M): 0.87/1.87 = 0.465 (0.74/1.74 = 0.425 to 0.5). That the sustainable catch is E × production is the steady-state relation (production = Z × biomass, catch = F × biomass), inferred here

transfer_efficiency.label: trophic transfer efficiency per level (Western Mediterranean food-web models)
